4. MEASURES PROPOSED BY THE APPLICANT TO ENHANCE THE ENVIRONMENT OR TO AVOID OR MITIGATE ADVERSE ENVIRON-MENTAL EFFECTS
4.1 PREVENTATIVE MEASURES AND MONITORING
A major impact of construction would be the adverse impacts of sedimentary material deposited in Howard Creek as a result of the erosion of land disturbed during construction. Boyne and Ingram (1975) recommend that, for the protection of benthic organisms, activities that would create excessive siltation should be kept to a minimum and be stringently controlled. They recommend continued monitoring of benthic organisms in Howard Creek during construction and for a period after project operation begins. Boyne and Ingram also suggest that the use of water releases to flush sediments from Howard Creek may be desirable if sediment accumulations are extensive. Simon and Dysart (1975) and Langdon, et al. (1976) suggest the use of storm flow augmentation after construction to help flush Howard Creek of sediment accumulations from construction and reduce the time required for recovery of Howard Creek.
The Applicant proposes to concentrate construction activities within the Bad Creek and West Bad Creek drainage basin to minimize adverse impacts on Howard Creek. Applicant estimates that nearly all the earth and rock fill material for construction of the dams could be obtained from within the reservoir basin area, thus eliminating the use of extensive areas west of South Carolina Route 171.
The permanent access road and temporary construction roads would be routed to minimize silt-laden runoff into existing streams and would emphasize a route within the Bad Creek drainage basin. Slopes would be seeded as soon as possible after land disturbances, and temporary roads would be regraded and p<sup>1</sup> inted as soon as they are no longer needed. Drainage control measures would be taken in areas where runoff would drain outside the Bad Creek drainage basin. The construction yard area would be located so as to take advantage of topographic features; natural slopes would be left undisturbed while other portions would be terraced, sloped, and drained to minimize siltation. Strips of existing trees and ground cover would be left intact. Contractor shops and staging areas would be situated in designated locations with consideration given to the environmental impact. Disturbed areas would be kept as small as possible
